intro: Google Docs has no native Mac app, so you use it in your browser. For grant work, Chrome is the safest choice on a Mac, because it supports offline editing. This page covers setup, shortcuts, comments, deadlines, and where Lazur helps. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that guides you through Docs. It does not do the clicks for you.
tldr: Google Docs runs in the browser on a Mac. Use Chrome or Edge if you need offline editing. Safari does not support it.
Learn ⌘/ first, then ⌘⌥M, ⌘⇧H, ⌥/ and ⌘ Enter. Those cover most grant draft moves.
Gemini comment tools need an eligible paid plan and edit access. They can take up to 15 days to appear.
In one vendor survey, 19 of 46 respondents said one grant application takes 10 to 20 hours. Plan your calendar around that range.
Lazur guides, points, explains, drafts and dictates. It does not click buttons or edit files for you. The Pro trial lasts 3 days and needs no credit card.

blocks.text: Most grant writers on a Mac use Google Docs in a browser tab. There is no official Google Docs app for macOS. An unofficial listing exists, but this guide does not verify it, so treat it with caution. Gemini has its own native Mac app, but that app is not Docs. Your week will look like this: find the funder's rules, draft against them, track the deadline, and send the file to a program officer. Google Docs handles the draft. The rest needs some setup.
Which browser to use for Google Docs on Mac

Chrome is the safest default for grant work on a Mac. It supports offline editing with a Google extension. Edge also works. Safari does not support offline Docs on a Mac, so you cannot keep editing a draft in Safari when the connection drops. Check the browser before you travel, not on the train.

blocks.text: Set up offline editing in Chrome on Mac

Offline editing matters when Wi-Fi drops during a deadline push, or when you draft on a train. Setup is quick. The steps below come from Google Drive Help. Drive menu labels change, so match the wording to what you see on your screen.

items: Open Chrome, not Safari and not a private window.
Install the Google Docs Offline extension, then turn it on.
Turn on offline access for Docs in your Google Drive settings.
To save several files at once, click the first file, then hold ⌘ and click the others.
Open each doc once while you are online, so it is ready when you leave.

blocks.text: Test it before you need it. Turn Wi-Fi off, open a doc, and type one sentence. Turn Wi-Fi back on and confirm the sentence saved. If your organization manages Chrome, an extension may need IT approval first. Ask before the week of a deadline, not during it.
Keyboard shortcuts for Google Docs on Mac grant drafts

Shortcuts save more time than most people expect. Grant drafts repeat the same moves: find a funder term, leave a comment, break a page before the budget. These are the Mac shortcuts from Google's keyboard list.

items: ⌘/ opens the full list of shortcuts in Docs. Start here.
⌘⇧H opens Find and replace. Use it when a funder changes a name, a date or a cap.
⌘⌥M inserts a comment on the selected text.
⌥/ opens Tool finder, a search box for menu items. Type what you want, then press Return.
⌘ Enter inserts a page break, useful before a budget or an appendix.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example. Your funder limits the narrative, and your draft runs long. Use ⌘⇧H to find each heading you might move or cut. Use ⌘ Enter to place breaks where a new section should start. Then open Tool finder with ⌥/ and search for word count, so you can check length before you export.
Screen reader and VoiceOver settings in Docs

This section is for people who use a screen reader. If you do not, skip ahead. Google's screen reader help says VoiceOver and Docs menu shortcuts both use Control+Option. That clash can block a shortcut you expect to work. Google suggests setting the VoiceOver modifier to Caps Lock. It also suggests using VoiceOver+Tab to pass a menu shortcut through. To turn on screen reader support in Docs, press ⌘⌥Z.
Build a grant template that matches the funder's order

Templates save hours, but only when their sections match the funder. A template is a starting point, not a substitute for the funder's guidelines. One paid example I checked is a Google Docs grant proposal template priced at $19.99. It runs about 15 pages with 10 sections, including a cover letter, a budget, methods and approaches, monitoring and evaluation, and sustainability. The seller describes it as 100% customizable in free Google Docs.

Make a copy before you change anything. Use File > Make a copy. Then rename each heading to match the funder's words, not your organization's words. A funder that asks for a statement of need will not find a heading called background useful. Keep the funder's exact terms in the headings, even when they feel clumsy.

Watch for the common failure. Many templates assume one funder's format. Private foundations often ask for different sections, a different order, or a different length. Keep a checklist of required items beside the template. Tick off each item before you export. Export as .docx only if the funder asks for it, and check the file in Word or Pages before you send it.
How long a grant application takes and how to plan for it

Plan with real numbers, and know where they come from. In a survey run by Instrumentl, 19 of 46 respondents said one grant application takes 10 to 20 hours. Ten said under 10 hours. Seven said 21 to 30 hours, seven said 31 to 40 hours, and three said 40 or more. The article's text rounds the 10 to 20 hour group to 40%. Use the counts instead. This is a small survey that asks about hours per application, not total time across a funder relationship.

A 2015 study looked at a different group. It surveyed 195 academics, 113 astronomers and 82 psychologists. The average proposal took 116 PI hours and 55 co-investigator hours. The authors estimate that is at least one month of full-time effort. Those are researchers writing research grants, so use the figure as context. It does not predict your own application. The study also found no link between writing time and whether a grant was funded.
Deciding which grants are worth the time

The same academic study offers a rule of thumb. Its authors estimate that funding rates below about 20% push at least half of active researchers away from federal grants. They suggest avoiding programs at or below 20% unless you have a better than baseline chance, or you plan to write two or more proposals a year. That is their estimate, not a measured result.

Use a simple check before you start. Find the funder's success rate on its own site. If you cannot find it, ask the program officer. If the rate is low and your organization fits the stated priorities poorly, skip the application. Spend those hours on a stronger fit. Write the decision down, so next year's team can see why you passed.
Comments and suggestions without losing track

Comments are where many drafts go wrong. A program officer leaves a note, a colleague suggests an edit, and nobody knows which version is current. Insert a comment with ⌘⌥M on the selected text, so the note stays tied to the words it covers. Write the question in the comment, not in the body of the draft.

Suggesting mode lets collaborators propose changes without overwriting your text. Turn it on from the editing mode menu, which sits near the Share button. Then accept or reject each suggestion. Only the lead writer should accept changes in the final week. Agree on that rule before the draft goes out.

Gemini can summarize long comment threads, but the feature has limits. Digital Trends reported on July 29, 2026 that Gemini's comment tools need an eligible paid plan. Gemini needs edit access, so viewers and commenters do not get it. Users approve every suggested change. The tools may take up to 15 days to appear on an account.

blocks.title: Labels change, so check your own screen
blocks.text: Google updates Docs often. The help pages behind this guide had no Mac-specific menu steps and no release date. Confirm each menu label on your own screen. Do not rely on a feature you have not seen working on your account.
Where Lazur helps in a Google Docs grant draft

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option and Command together, to ask about anything on screen. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. It answers out loud. When you ask where something is, it draws a circle and a label around it.

Use it for the parts of grant work that break your focus. Ask what a funder's section means in plain words. Ask where the totals row sits in your budget table. Ask for a first draft of a boilerplate paragraph. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate Docs for you. When you ask how to do something, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.

Dictation works in Docs too. Hold fn, speak, and release. The text lands at your cursor, cleaned up and formatted. Snippets store boilerplate, such as your organization's mission statement. A personal dictionary holds names and acronyms, such as a funder's name or a program code, so they come out right. Clipboard slots keep budget figures ready to paste.
Research funders and track deadlines with Lazur

Research is the slow part of many grant jobs. Lazur can run research in its own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use it to review a funder's recent awards or to read guidelines spread across several pages. Check every figure in the report against the funder's own site before you cite it.

Deadlines are the second job. Instrumentl's description of a grant writer's day lists researching grants and guidelines, drafting, tracking application steps, letters of inquiry, funding reports, and prospect research. That is a lot of dates. Put each one in Apple Reminders or Calendar as soon as you find it. You can ask Lazur to add it by voice, then check the date once more.
Mistakes that cost grant writers time on Mac

items: Working in Safari and expecting offline access. Safari does not support it. Switch to Chrome or Edge first.
Opening a doc in a private window for offline work. Private browsing blocks offline use.
Typing in Editing mode when the lead writer wants suggestions. Check the mode before you type.
Assuming Gemini comment summaries work on any account. They need an eligible paid plan and edit access.
Keeping a template's section order without checking the funder's guidelines.
Pressing Control+Option shortcuts while VoiceOver is on, then wondering why Docs ignores them.
Using the 116 hour academic figure to plan a grant. It came from researchers, not grant writers.

blocks.text: Pick one fix per week. Small habits add up over a season of applications. Start with the browser, because a wrong browser breaks every other step.
What Lazur sends and stores

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. Those files are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Grant drafts often hold budgets and program data. Check your funder's confidentiality rules before you share any draft with an AI tool, Lazur included.
Lazur pricing and the free trial

Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts the first time you open the app. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, and includes 250 AI actions. Power costs $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. See [pricing](/pricing) or [download the app](/download).
A short setup plan for this week

items: Install Chrome, then the Google Docs Offline extension. Test it with Wi-Fi off.
Make a copy of your template. Rename the headings to match the funder's words.
Learn ⌘/ first. Then add ⌘⌥M and ⌘⇧H.
Put every deadline in Apple Reminders today.
Try Lazur on the three tasks that waste the most time in your week.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Docs runs in a browser on a Mac, such as Chrome, Edge or Safari. An unofficial listing exists, but it was not verified for this guide. Gemini has a separate native Mac app, but that is not Docs.

faq.question: Can I use Google Docs offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, in Chrome or Edge. Install and turn on the Google Docs Offline Chrome extension, then turn on offline access in Drive. Do not use private browsing, and Safari does not support offline Docs on a Mac.

faq.question: Which keyboard shortcut shows all Google Docs shortcuts on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘/. Google's keyboard shortcut list also shows Find and replace as ⌘⇧H, comments as ⌘⌥M, and Tool finder as ⌥/. Use Tool finder when you cannot remember a menu item.

faq.question: Why do my Docs shortcuts not work with VoiceOver on?
faq.answer: VoiceOver and Docs menu shortcuts both use Control+Option, so they can clash. Google suggests setting the VoiceOver modifier to Caps Lock, or using VoiceOver+Tab to pass a menu shortcut through.

faq.question: Do Gemini comment summaries work in every Google Docs account?
faq.answer: No. Digital Trends reported on July 29, 2026 that Gemini's comment tools need an eligible paid plan and edit access. Viewers and commenters do not get them, and the tools may take up to 15 days to appear.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my grant document for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It answers questions out loud, points at things on screen, guides you one click at a time, drafts text, and dictates text you speak while holding fn.

faq.question: How long does a grant application take to write?
faq.answer: A vendor survey of 46 people found 19 said 10 to 20 hours. That survey asks about hours per application, so treat it as a rough guide. A 2015 academic study found 116 PI hours per proposal, but it covered researchers, not grant writers.

faq.question: Is there a free trial for Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts the first time you open the app. Lazur runs on macOS only, and Windows is planned, not available.
